title.en: Practical 3: Melting point of wax (cooling curve)

text.en: Wax stays at one temperature while it freezes, and that is how we find its melting point.

The aim is to determine the melting point of wax using a cooling curve. The principle is latent heat: the heat needed to change a unit mass from one state to another without changing temperature.
Melt the wax in a warm water bath, remove it when fully melted, dry the tube and bury it in sand. Record the temperature every 30 seconds while the liquid becomes solid. Watch for a constant temperature at which liquid and solid exist together.
Plot temperature against time. The flat portion of the cooling curve gives the melting point of wax. Apparatus includes beaker, burner, thermometer, boiling tube, stand, tripod, stopwatch and a bowl of sand.

problem.en: Write the record for 'Practical 3: Melting point of wax (cooling curve)' in three steps.

text.en: Melt the wax in a water bath.
Cool it in sand and note the temperature every 30 s.
Read the constant temperature as the melting point.

prompt.en: A friend says The temperature keeps falling while wax solidifies. How will you reply?

requiredIdeas.en: It stays constant for a while.
That constant value is the melting point.
